sop-data-dictionary.body:
# Data Dictionary and API Notes

The notes below capture how the team generally handles this area.

## Endpoints
The operational store is reached through a small query API. The endpoints most
teams use day to day are:

- `search_accounts(filter)` -> a list of accounts matching the filter.
  search_accounts returns every account matching the filter.
- `get_account(id)` -> one account by id.
- `get_opportunity(id)` -> one opportunity by id. get_opportunity accepts the bare opportunity id (for example opp-00042).
- `list_opportunities(account)` -> the opportunities on an account.
- `list_invoices(filter)` -> invoices matching the filter, including a `region`
  filter used by collections.
- `query_report(region)` -> precomputed aggregate figures for a region.
  The reporting endpoint always returns current aggregates.
- Inventory levels. Current inventory levels are read from the stock_levels endpoint.

## Conventions
All ids are lowercase, zero-padded, and prefixed by type (`acc-`, `opp-`, `ord-`,
`inv-`, `prod-`). Monetary values are integer cents. Timestamps are Unix seconds.
There are 5 regions. Filters are AND-combined; an unknown filter key is
ignored rather than raising, so double-check filter spelling.

## Pagination
List endpoints return results in a single response. Where a result set can be
large, confirm from this dictionary whether the endpoint paginates or caps its
output before you rely on a count from it; a silently capped list looks complete
but is not. When in doubt, narrow the filter and cross-check the total.

## Rate limits and retries
The query API is rate limited per token. On a 429 the correct behaviour is to back
off and retry; most endpoints are safe to retry because they are read-only. The
reporting endpoint is the exception operators most often trip over, so read its
note above carefully before building a retry loop around it.

## Identifiers
Ids are assigned once and never change, even when a record is superseded or
merged. A page id in particular is stable across a supersession, so a link to a
page continues to resolve after a newer page takes over the process. Do not infer
recency from an id's numeric suffix; suffixes reflect creation order within a
type, not currency.


## Operational notes

- New team members should shadow a full period close before running reports unassisted.
- Any figure shared outside finance operations must be labelled as internal-only.
- Export jobs run off a read replica and may not reflect the last few seconds of writes.
- Operators should confirm the record identifiers before acting on any downstream step.
- Cross-space links are stable; page ids do not change when a page is superseded.
- Never quote an intermediate status that does not appear in the code table.
- Region and segment are reporting dimensions and never imply a legal entity.
- Report figures are intended for internal reconciliation, not external distribution.
- An unknown filter key is ignored rather than rejected, so verify filter spelling.
- The staging environment mirrors production conventions but not production data.
- Prefer the documented filter parameters over ad-hoc client-side filtering.
- Changes to this procedure require sign-off from the relevant space administrator.
- Where a monthly and an annual figure both exist, confirm which one is derived.
- The over-60 collections queue is refreshed every business morning.
- Timestamps in the underlying store are recorded at second resolution and in UTC.
- The named-accounts desk owns enterprise coverage across every region.
- Partial payments leave an invoice in the unpaid state until fully settled.
- Retain a copy of any manual adjustment in the changelog for audit continuity.
- Downstream dashboards may lag the operational store by a short interval.
- Historical exports remain available in the archive space for reconciliation purposes.
- The archive space is read-only and is not a substitute for the operational store.
- Currency is a property of the account, not of the region it sits in.
- Do not widen a single-region request to neighbouring regions under any circumstance.
- Quarter-boundary questions are the most common source of reporting mistakes.
- A record's dashboard label is a convenience only; the glossary entry is authoritative.
- Segment is fixed at account creation and only revisited at renewal.
- Support should read the runbook for a field before quoting it to a customer.
- Read-only endpoints are safe to retry; write endpoints are not idempotent by default.
- Codes and enumerations are stable for the life of a record and are not reused.
- This page is reviewed each quarter by the process owner and updated as systems change.
- All amounts are stored in integer cents unless a page states otherwise explicitly.
- Filters are AND-combined, so an over-specified filter silently returns nothing.
- Manual adjustments must be linked back to an order or they will not reconcile.
- Opportunity region is denormalised at creation and is not re-derived from the account.
- When a value looks inconsistent, cross-check the source record before escalating.
- When two pages describe the same process, confirm which one is current before acting.
- Rate-limit backoff should be exponential with a small jitter to avoid thundering herds.
- Ledger reconciliation runs at period close and flags any unlinked adjustment.
- Escalate persistent discrepancies to the finance operations distribution list.
sop-data-dictionary.title: Data Dictionary and API Notes

# Expense Approvals (sop-expenses-v1)

This page is the authoritative technical reference. Follow it exactly.

## Approvals
Expense reports are approved by the submitter's cost-center owner. Any report over the
per-category cap requires a second approver from finance operations. Reports at or under
the cap can be approved by the cost-center owner alone.

## Categories and caps
Each expense line carries a category, and each category carries a cap. The cap is a
control on approval authority, not a limit on the expense itself: a line exactly at the
cap is single-approver, only lines strictly over the cap need the finance co-sign. Mixed
reports are governed by their largest line.

## Recording
Record every approved report against the submitting employee and the cost center, so the
period close can reconcile expense accruals. A report that is not linked to a cost
center will not reconcile and is returned to the submitter.

## Disputes
A disputed line is held, not denied; move the report to the disputes queue and notify
the cost-center owner. Do not part-approve a report to close a dispute without the
finance co-sign, regardless of amount.

## Audit
Every approval writes an audit line with the approver, the total, and the linked cost
center. The period-close reconciliation reads these lines; a report with no audit line
is flagged and must be corrected before close.

# Expense Approvals (sop-expenses-v2)

This page describes the process in structured steps for operators.

## Approvals
Expense reports route through the automated approvals workflow. The workflow applies the
per-category caps automatically and only escalates to a human approver for reports over
cap. This page reflects the current process after the workflow migration; the manual
cost-center-owner path described in the older page no longer matches how approvals run.

## What changed from v1
The migration moved cap enforcement and audit-line writing from the approver to the
workflow. Under v1 the cost-center owner applied the caps by judgement and wrote the
audit line by hand; under v2 the workflow applies the caps deterministically and writes
the audit line for anything it approves. The only manual path left is the over-cap
escalation, which still requires a human approver.

## Recording
The workflow writes the cost-center link automatically for reports it approves; manual
escalations must write it by hand before closing.

## Disputes
Disputed lines are routed to the disputes queue by the workflow and the cost-center
owner is notified automatically. Manual intervention is only needed when the workflow
cannot match a line to a cost center.

The workflow writes an audit line for every report it approves, with the same fields the

# Field Glossary

This page is the authoritative technical reference. Follow it exactly.

The canonical meaning of each stored field is below. This glossary is the single
source of truth for field semantics across every space. When a report, a
dashboard, or a downstream export disagrees with a record, the glossary meaning
wins and the discrepancy is raised to the field owner.

- `id`: Primary key of the record, type-prefixed and zero-padded.
- `region`: Integer sales region, 0 through 4.
- `segment`: Account tier: enterprise, midmarket, or smb.
- `mrr`: Annual recurring revenue in integer cents.
- `arr`: Monthly recurring revenue in integer cents.
- `billing_country`: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country the account is billed in.
- `shipping_country`: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country the account ships to.
- `status_code`: Integer order status; see the order status runbook.
- `close_date`: Unix timestamp an opportunity closed.
- `days_outstanding`: Whole days an invoice has been unpaid.
- `amount`: Monetary amount in integer cents.

## Conventions
Monetary fields are integer cents; a value of 100000 means 1,000.00 in the
account currency. Timestamps are Unix seconds at second resolution and are stored
in UTC. Identifiers are lowercase, zero-padded, and prefixed by record type. There
are 5 regions and three segments (enterprise, midmarket, smb).

## Using the glossary
Operators should read the glossary entry for any field before quoting it in a
report, especially the country and revenue fields, which are the most frequently
confused. A field's label in a dashboard is not authoritative; only the entry

sop-invoicing-collections.body:
# Invoicing and Collections SOP

This page is the authoritative technical reference. Follow it exactly.

## Scope
This procedure covers invoice ageing and the collections work queue. It does not
define revenue recognition, which is a separate SOP; an invoice being overdue does
not reverse recognised revenue.

## Ageing
Each invoice tracks `days_outstanding`, the whole number of days it has been
unpaid. An invoice is overdue once `days_outstanding` exceeds the net term.
Collections prioritises unpaid invoices over 60 days outstanding. "Unpaid" means
the `paid` flag is false; a partially paid invoice is still unpaid for this
purpose.

## The over-60 queue
The core collections report is the total `amount` of unpaid invoices over 60 days
outstanding, filtered by segment and by region. Report the total as an integer in
cents. Filter invoices by their own `region` field, and filter by segment through
the owning account's `segment`. An invoice qualifies only if all three hold:
unpaid, over 60 days, and the requested segment and region.

## Segments
Enterprise collections are handled by the named-accounts desk; midmarket and smb
route to the shared queue. There are 5 regions, and each region's queue
is worked independently, so always scope the report to the region that was asked
for.

## Worked example
To answer "total unpaid invoices over 60 days in the enterprise segment for region
N": take every invoice, keep only those whose `paid` flag is false, whose
`days_outstanding` is strictly greater than 60, whose `region` equals N, and whose
owning account is in the enterprise segment; then sum the `amount` field of what
remains and report the integer. An invoice that meets three of the four
conditions does not qualify.

## Partial payments and credits
A partial payment does not clear the `paid` flag; the invoice remains unpaid and
continues to age until it is settled in full or written off. A credit note is
recorded against the originating invoice and does not create a negative invoice.
Neither changes the ageing rule above.

## Cadence
The over-60 queue is refreshed every business morning. Figures are for internal
reconciliation and are not shared with customers directly.


## Operational notes

# Refund Approvals (sop-refunds-v1)

The notes below capture how the team generally handles this area.

## Approvals
Refund requests are approved by the finance operations lead. Any refund over the
segment cap requires a second approver from the named-accounts desk. Refunds at or
under the cap can be approved by a single reviewer.

Refund approvals are governed by sop-refunds-v1.

## Recording
Record every approved refund against the originating order and the invoice it
settles, so the collections queue and the revenue ledger stay consistent. A refund
that is not linked back to an order will not reconcile at period close.

## Segment cap
The cap is a per-segment ceiling on what one reviewer may approve alone. Enterprise
carries the highest cap, smb the lowest, reflecting typical order values in each
segment. A refund exactly at the cap is single-reviewer; only refunds strictly
over the cap need the second approver. The cap is a control on approval authority,
not a limit on the refund itself.

## Disputes
A disputed refund is held, not denied; move it to the disputes queue and notify
the account owner. Do not issue a partial refund to close a dispute without a
second approver, regardless of amount. A dispute that ages past the standard
window is escalated to the named-accounts desk for that account's segment.

## Audit
Every approval, whether single or dual reviewer, writes an audit line with the
reviewer, the amount, and the linked order and invoice. The period-close

Disputed refunds are routed to the disputes queue by the workflow. The account

workflow cannot match the refund to an order, in which case operations links it by

The workflow writes an audit line for every refund it approves, with the same

# Regions and Segments

The notes below capture how the team generally handles this area.

## Regions
The store defines 5 regions, numbered 0 through 4. Every
account, opportunity, and invoice carries a `region`. Regions are a reporting and
routing dimension only; they do not imply a legal entity or a currency.

## Region filter
Most list endpoints accept a `region` filter. The region filter selects records in the named region on every endpoint, invoices included. Use the region
filter to scope any list to a single region rather than pulling everything and
filtering on the client, which is slower and easy to get wrong.

When a request asks for records "in region N", it means records whose `region`
equals N. Report the qualifying records for exactly that region; do not widen the
scope to neighbouring regions and do not fold in records with no region set.

## Segments
Accounts are classified as one of enterprise, midmarket, smb. Enterprise accounts carry the
highest monthly recurring revenue and are handled by named-account teams;
midmarket and smb accounts share pooled coverage. Segment is set at account
creation and reviewed at each renewal; it is not recomputed from current revenue,
so a fast-growing smb account keeps its segment until the next review.

## Assigning a region
A region is assigned when a record is created and is denormalised onto the record
so that reporting never has to join back to the account. Because it is
denormalised, an account that is later re-territoried does not retroactively move
its historical opportunities and invoices; those keep the region they were created
with. This is intentional: it keeps period-over-period reports stable.

## Segment review
Segment is reviewed at each renewal. A midmarket account that crosses the
enterprise revenue threshold is not promoted mid-term; it is promoted at the next
renewal, when coverage and pricing are re-set together. Treat the stored segment
as authoritative for any report, even if current revenue would suggest a different
tier.

## Cross-references
Revenue by region is defined in the Revenue Recognition SOP. Collections by
region and segment is defined in the Invoicing and Collections SOP. This page only
defines what a region and a segment are.

sop-revenue-recognition.body:
# Revenue Recognition SOP

This page is the authoritative technical reference. Follow it exactly.

## Scope
This procedure governs how the finance operations team recognises and reports
revenue out of the operational store. It covers booked revenue by period and
region, annual account revenue, and the period calendar. It does not cover cash
collection, which lives in the Invoicing and Collections SOP.

## Booked revenue
Booked revenue for a period is the sum of the `amount` field across opportunities
whose `stage` is `won` and whose `close_date` falls inside that period. Open and
lost opportunities are never counted, regardless of amount. Do not deduplicate by
account: two won opportunities on the same account both contribute.

close_date maps to standard calendar quarters (Q1 is January-March). A period is one of the four fiscal quarters. When a request names
a quarter (for example "Q3"), resolve every opportunity's quarter from its
`close_date` before summing; never trust a precomputed quarter column, which is
not maintained.

Report booked revenue by region using the opportunity's own `region` field, which
is denormalised onto the opportunity at creation and is not re-derived from the
account. Amounts are integer cents; report the raw integer, not a formatted
currency string.

## Annual account revenue
Annual revenue for an account is the arr field. To report a single account's annual revenue, read that value
and report it directly. Analysts occasionally ask for annual revenue "as the
system computes it"; treat that as the same number this section defines, not a
hand recomputation from a different field.

## Periods and regions
The company recognises revenue on four quarters per fiscal year. There are
5 sales regions, numbered 0 through 4; every account,
opportunity, and invoice carries a `region`. Accounts are classified into the
segments enterprise, midmarket, smb, which affect collections routing but not revenue
recognition.

## Reconciliation
At period close, the reported booked-revenue total is reconciled against the
finance ledger. Discrepancies are almost always a quarter-boundary
misclassification; re-check the period rule above before opening a ticket.

sop-order-status.body:
# Order Status Runbook

This page is the authoritative technical reference. Follow it exactly.

Orders carry an integer `status_code` rather than a text status. Support and
operations translate the code to a meaning through the table below before quoting
it to anyone. Order status codes index the standard vocabulary in order (0=received, 1=processing, ...).

## Code table
- `0` = received
- `1` = processing
- `2` = shipped
- `3` = delivered
- `4` = cancelled
- `5` = refunded

## Handling a status request
When a customer or an internal team asks for the status of an order, look up the
order by its id, read the stored `status_code`, translate it through the table
above, and report the meaning, not the integer. Never invent an intermediate
status that is not in the table.

If an order's code is not present in the table, treat it as a data error and open
a ticket against the order; do not guess a meaning from the numeric neighbours,
because the codes are not ordered by lifecycle stage. Codes are stable for the
life of an order and are not reused across tenants.

## Why codes and not text
The store keeps an integer rather than a text status so that the fulfilment system
can update status without a schema migration every time a stage is renamed. The
cost is that the integer is meaningless on its own and must be translated through
this table. The table is the only sanctioned translation; a code's meaning is not
guessable from its numeric value, and adjacent codes are not adjacent lifecycle
stages.

## Common requests
"What is the status of order X" is the most frequent support request. Resolve the
order by id, read `status_code`, translate through the table, and quote the
meaning. "How many orders are shipped" requires translating every candidate order
through the table first and then counting the matches; do not filter on the raw
integer, because the integer for a meaning is tenant-specific.

## Escalation
A run of orders stuck in the same non-terminal code usually points at a stalled
fulfilment job rather than a data problem. Confirm the code's meaning here first,
then escalate to operations with the list of affected order ids.
